Frame: top rail y~184-193 (x 208->884), a right border column x~883 running the whole height, a mid rail y~447-475 broken by one hop, and a bottom ground rail y~840-854 (x 47->881).

JUDGEMENT CALLS
  S13 (481,452) deg5 (really a 4-way + a duplicate branch), dot=1.8 hop=0.0 -> called JUNCTION (agrees with the default). Branches: e24 up to the +6V arrow stem, e27 left to R#7, e31 right to R#9, e32 down to BJT#10's emitter. The zoom at 10x shows the +6V stem running dead straight through the mid rail with no widening and no detour. Decisive evidence is the drafter's own idiom: this sheet contains exactly two genuine wire-over-wire crossings (S18 at 760,474 with hop score 48.8 and S37 at 561,746 with hop score 40.6) and BOTH carry a large, unmistakable semicircular jog. S13 has none, so it is a real node. Consequence of the other reading (crossing): n7 would split into {+6V, #10.emitter} and {R#7.t1, R#9.t0}, giving 17 nets and turning the R7/R9 pair into a bare 2-terminal series link with no third connection.
  S19 (883,476) deg4, dot=1.5 hop=0.0 -> called JUNCTION (agrees with the default). Branches: e20 up to BJT#4's emitter, e42 left along the mid rail from R#9, e43 right to the +5V arrow, e46 down the right border to #15/#20. Same argument: a plain, straight 4-way with no jog on a sheet where every real crossing is jogged, and the resulting node (+5V feeding an NPN emitter and two NPN/PNP collectors) is the obvious intent. Consequence of the other reading (crossing): n5 would split into {R#9.t1, +5V} and {#4.emitter, #15.emitter, #20.collector}, leaving the +5V arrow feeding nothing but a resistor.
  S18 (760,474) deg4 -> CROSSING (agrees with the default, hop=48.8). The diode column (Diode#5 bottom -> Diode#11 top) makes a big S-jog around the horizontal mid rail. Junction here would merge n6 (the mid-point of the two series diodes) into n5, shorting Diode#5 to the +5V rail and destroying the diode stack.
  S37 (561,746) deg4 -> CROSSING (agrees with the default, hop=40.6). R#16's ground leg (the x~555 column) jogs around the horizontal wire that carries BJT#10/#19 collectors across to BJT#21's base. Junction here would tie n8 to ground, shorting out R#16 and grounding two collectors and a base.
  BRIDGE B23 (231,840)->(234,837), flagged CRITICAL: KEPT (not dropped). inkmap shows the left half of the bottom rail ending at x=230,y=840-841, BJT#17's emitter stroke descending at x=234-236 and landing at y=838-840, and the right half of the rail resuming at x=237,y=840 - three strokes meeting inside a 6 px box with only 3-5 px of thin/faded pen between them. The 14x zoom shows one continuous (if faint) horizontal line through the meeting point with the emitter wire curving into it. Dropping the bridge would strand R#18's bottom and BJT#14's collector on a 2-terminal net with no ground, and would leave the drawn bottom rail cut in half for no visible reason.
  All remaining CRITICAL sites are unambiguous degree-3 T's (a wire ending on another wire) and were explicitly recorded as junctions: S3 (504,184, +15V stem onto the top rail), S6 (211,268, +10V lead onto the R1/R3 column), S10 (212,448, R#7's lead onto the R3/#12 column), S26 (882,613, BJT#15's emitter lead onto the right border), S27 (42,625, BJT#14's base lead onto the +3V/R18 column), S28 (752,654, BJT#15's base lead onto the diode column), S29 (483,685, BJT#19's collector onto the #10-collector column), S40 (126,840), S41 (552,845), S42 (483,847), S43 (755,849), S44 (881,854) - the last five are leads landing on the bottom ground rail.
  Non-critical sites left at their defaults: S1/S2 ('+15V' text over the arrow), S7 ('15kOhm' text on R#3), S8 ('+6V' text), S11/S12 ('+5V' text), S14/S15/S20 ('150 Ohm' text on R#7), S23 (a 2 px stub at BJT#10's emitter port), S25 ('+3V' text), S30/S33/S34/S35 ('50kOhm' text on R#18). None of them changes the netlist. 24 gap bridges found; only B23 matters and it is kept.

PORT / PIN-ORDER FIXES
  #6 V-DC (+6V arrow): t0 -> p1 (481,443), the bottom of the arrow's stem, instead of p0 (498,409) which is the right barb of the arrowhead / the '+' of the '+6V' label. This is what fixed the summary's 'net n7 touches only 1 terminal' error: with p1 the supply lands on the R#7/R#9/#10-emitter node as drawn.
  Four PNP transistors had collector and emitter swapped. Every BJT on this sheet is drawn with a vertical base bar, a base lead leaving it sideways, and two diagonals to an upper and a lower terminal; the emitter is the diagonal carrying the arrowhead. At 12x and 22x zoom the arrowhead sits on the LOWER diagonal of every NPN (#4, #17, #19, #20, #21 - already correct as collector,base,emitter) and on the UPPER diagonal of every PNP (#10, #12, #14, #15). Required order is (collector, base, emitter):
    #10 BJT-PNP (488,549), base bar on the RIGHT: t0->p0 (477,587 collector, lower diagonal, plain - verified at 22x), t1->p2 (512,550 base), t2->p1 (479,509 emitter, upper diagonal, arrowhead at ~(488,530)). Emitter now sits on the +6V node and the collector drives #19/#21 - textbook PNP.
    #12 BJT-PNP (206,546), base bar on the left: t0->p1 (221,585 collector), t1->p2 (182,544 base), t2->p0 (218,505 emitter, arrowhead on the upper diagonal at ~(203,530)).
    #14 BJT-PNP (120,622): t0->p0 (129,657 collector, runs to the ground rail), t1->p1 (98,627 base, fed from +3V), t2->p2 (131,586 emitter, arrowhead on the upper diagonal at ~(122,610)).
    #15 BJT-PNP (812,655): t0->p0 (825,688 collector, drives #20's base), t1->p2 (784,655 base), t2->p1 (823,622 emitter, arrowhead at ~(811,643), runs to the +5V rail).
  The five NPNs and all two-terminal parts were checked and left alone. The three resistor warnings (#1 port at (221,217), #3 ports at (221,335)/(227,344), #9 port at (590,482)) are all '15kOhm'/'150 Ohm' label strokes crossing the box edge; the terminals already point at the real leads.

CLASSES: all 23 checked against the drawing; all correct. The four PNPs and six NPNs are distinguishable by arrow direction relative to the base bar and all match their COCO labels. Nothing left unresolved; no merges, no unconnected components.
